C0.quote: Different rules have been used to aggregate participants’ votes.

C1.quote: a theoretical and empirical study of the worst-case guarantees
C1.note: Worst-case utilitarian and representation guarantees. AX covers the guarantees for the class of EJR rules. SI uses the Euclidean and party-list datasets. EM uses Pabulib data from Poland.

C2.2.quote: the set of projects that voter 𝑖 approves.

C2.3.quote: citizens vote on which of the projects they would like to fund
C2.3.note: Utility is also attributed to voters: 'each voter get a utility of 1'.

C2.4.quote: they may strategize as they wish.
C2.4.note: There is no separate notation. The introduction says outright that voters may strategize, so what they submit may differ from the projects they would like to fund. This meets the textual criterion for DIST, although the formal model applies the rules to the approval profile directly.

C5.1.note: Social welfare, representation and EJR are all used in results.

C9.2.quote: they may strategize as they wish.
C9.2.note: Claims about citizens' satisfaction and rule recommendations need submitted approvals to equal voters' held attitudes, which is never stated. The paper even notes that voters may strategize. The utility link (1 per approved project) is stated.

C2.4.reason: The codebook allows DIST on text saying submitted inputs may differ from held attitudes, and 'they may strategize as they wish' is such text.

C6.VOT.reason: The codebook counts a type as present when it takes an action even if that action is fixed, and voters submitting approval sets is such an action.
